title: WPSS/1923/2019 of NARESH CHAND SHARMA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
WPSS No. 1923 of 2019
Hon'ble Lok Pal Singh, J.
Mr. Sanpreet Singh Ajmani, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. N.P. Sah and Mr. Sushil Vasishtha,
Standing Counsel for the State.
By means of present petition, petitioner has
sought following reliefs:
"(i) Issue writ, order, rule or direction in the
nature of mandamus directing the respondents to
reckon the period served by the petitioner as 'Ansh
Kaleen Nalkoop Chalak' for computing the qualifying
service for purpose of grant of pension and other
retiral benefits in the light of judgment rendered by
the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Habib
Khan Ors. Vs. State of Uttarakhand & ors."
 (ii) Issue writ, order, rule or direction in the
nature of mandamus directing the respondents to
grant pension and all necessary and consequential
benefits to the petitioner alongwith 18% interest per
annum or with such rate which this Hon'ble court
deem fit and proper till the date of actual payment,
in the interest of justice.
(iii) Issue, writ, order, rule or direction in the
nature of mandamus to allow the benefit of time
scale by counting their entire length of service in the
work charge establishment and as an muster roll
employee alongwith all consequential benefit thereof
and calculate the aforesaid period of their service
rendered as a muster roll employee and work charge
establishment for all the practical purposes
including service benefits.
(iv) Issue, writ, rule or direction in the nature
of mandamus to award suitable compensation of Rs.
5.00 Lacs to each of the petitioner for the
constitutional tort of the respondents depriving the
petitioner from their legitimate right to pension."
Initially the petitioner was appointed on the
post of Nalkoop Chalak in the Irrigation
Department, Tubewell Division, Bazpur as work
charge employee in the year 1993. Petitioner was
regularized on the post of Nalkoop Chalak in the
year 2016. Thereafter, he was superannuated
from the services on 31.01.2017. Grievance of the
petitioner is that the respondent department has
not considered his service as work charge
employee for the purpose of granting him retiral
dues.
Learned counsel for the petitioner would
submit that since the petitioner retired from
services after completing almost 24 years,

therefore, he is entitled to all post retiral dues but
such benefits were not given to him on the pretext
that petitioner did not have qualifying service for
receiving post retiral dues. He would further
submit that though the petitioner was engaged on
temporary basis but subsequently he was
conferred with regular status on 14.03.2016,
therefore, now for the purpose of post retiral dues
and qualifying service entire service is to be taken
into consideration. He referred the Government
order issued by Secretary, Government of
Uttarakhand on 11.08.2020, which has been
passed in compliance of Hon'ble Apex Court's
judgment dated 02.09.2019, wherein the Hon'ble
Apex Court has decided the similar controversy.
In the said G.O., the operative portion of the
judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court has also been
referred, which reads as follows:
"In view of reading down Rule 3(8) of the
U.P. Retirement Benefits Rules 1961, we hold
that services rendered in the work charged
establishment shall be treated as qualifying
service under the aforesaid rule for grant of
pension. The arrears of pension shall be
confined to three years only before the date of
the order. Let the admissible benefits be paid
accordingly within three months. Resultantly,
the appeals filed by the employees are allowed
and filed by the State are dismissed."
It is further stated in the aforesaid
Government order that in compliance of the order
of Hon'ble Apex Court dated 02.02.2019 the
service rendered by the employee in the work
charge establishment as well as Industrial
establishment shall be treated as qualifying
service for the purpose of grant of pension.
Learned counsel for the petitioner would
submit that the in view of the aforesaid
Government order dated 11.08.2020, the
petitioner is also entitled for the same benefit. He
would further submit that the case of the
petitioner is covered by the decision of the Hon'ble
Supreme Court in the case of Prem Singh v. State
of Uttar Pradesh and Others, reported (2020) 3
SCC 54. The relevant paragraph-36 of the above
decision reads as under :-
"In view of reading down Rule 3(8) of the U.P.
Retirement Benefits Rules, 1961, we hold that

services rendered in the work-charged
establishment shall be treated as qualifying service
under the aforesaid rule for grant of pension. The
arrears of pension shall be confined to three years
only before the date of the order. Let the admissible
benefits be paid accordingly within three months.
Resultantly, the appeals filed by the employees are
allowed and filed by the State are dismissed."
Learned counsel for the petitioner would
further submit that Honble Apex Court in Habib
Khan vs. State of Uttarakhand and
others reported in 2019(10)SCC 542 has directed
for counting the services rendered in work charge
establishment for the purposes of grant of pension
along with all necessary and consequential
benefits.
Considering the facts and circumstances
that have been brought on record and in view of
the dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in the
judgments (supra), I dispose of the writ petition
with the directions to the respondents/authorities
concerned to decide and consider the claim of the
petitioner in the light of Government order dated
11.08.2020 and as per the dictum of Hon'ble
Apex Court in the judgments (supra) as
expeditiously as possible preferably within a
period of eight weeks from the date of production
of certified copy of this order.
All pending applications stand disposed of.
No order as to costs.
 (Lok Pal Singh, J.)
mamta 16.12.2020
